title: COB duct/pipe catalog component manifest
description: One manifest per catalog component. Every dimension must trace to a source, and every size a component claims to support must exist in cob-l4-duct-inventory.json (or be explicitly standard-derived). Enumerate, do not invent.

id.description: kebab-case, stable, used as the instancing key

cob_part_name.description: The designer's own block name from the M-HVAC-DUCT legend, verbatim, when one exists. Naming authority only -- NOT a dimensional authority (see CAD-REQUIREMENTS.md 9a).

params.description: Parametric inputs. Ranges must be justified by supported_sizes or by a standard.

derived_from.description: Formula when the value is not free, e.g. 'length >= 1.5 * delta_w' (SMACNA 1:3).

supported_sizes.description: The FINITE set this component covers. Validated against cob-l4-duct-inventory.json.

basis.description: The 46-family label set. NEVER rect_families_reconstructed (35) -- it drops the four largest ducts on the level and 40x20.

certainty.description: CERT = measured in the pinned artifact (L4-full.json sha 7533dccb) or the raw DXF. INFER = read off a name/label whose geometry is unverified. STANDARD = from a published standard, NOT from COB data -- mandatory for every pipe component.

standard.description: e.g. 'SMACNA HVAC Duct Construction Standards' or 'ASME B36.10M'

license.description: Required for any external mesh (design3d Rule 8). Omit for procedural geometry.

origin.description: where the local origin sits, e.g. 'inlet face centre'

ports.description: Connection points, so a run can snap and instance rather than build ad-hoc geometry. Port ids are OPEN (in/out/branch/b1/b2/neck/...) -- a component is not a two-port pipeline; crossRect has b1+b2. `dir` is a free unit vector, NOT axis-aligned -- a 45 deg elbow emits [cos t,0,sin t] and any validator restricting dir to the six axes rejects every non-90 deg fitting. `shape` is PER PORT, never per component -- vavBox and transitionRectRound are round-in / rect-out. A port may also declare `mating`: contact_type plus embed_depth, which is what makes an instanced assembly FIT rather than merely align. Adapted from nave-panccadia's equipment specs (parent_socket / contact_type / embed_depth / gap_tolerance) — note that its three uses there are FURNITURE joints, a leg into a foot cup, so the pattern is borrowed but the HVAC contact types and values are ours and carry their own provenance.

id.description: open set: in, out, branch, b1, b2, neck, ...

pos.description: component-local metres; origin at the inlet port face, +X flow, +Y up, +Z lateral

dir.description: unit vector pointing OUT of the component; arbitrary direction, not axis-aligned. Two ports mate when dirA = -dirB and sections agree.

d.description: round only, metres. For PIPE this is the B36.10M OUTSIDE diameter, not the NPS label (NPS 4 is 4.500 in, not 4.000 in). For round DUCT the nominal IS the diameter -- duct and pipe do not share a size convention.

mating.description: HOW this port joins its neighbour, as distinct from WHERE it is. The port fields align two parts; these decide whether the assembly FITS. Concretely: a slip-fit or socket joint makes the assembled length SHORTER than the sum of the part lengths by embed_depth, so a run instanced by butting ports together is longer than the real duct, once per joint. On a network with hundreds of fittings that is a quantity error, not a rendering nicety.

contact_type.description: flange  — bolted face to face, no overlap (ASME B16.5 pipe flanges; TDC/TDF duct flanges). slip-fit — one end slides inside the other by embed_depth (sheet-metal duct into a fitting). socket  — a receiving socket overlaps the inserted end (ASME B16.11 socket-weld pipe fittings; a round tap into a trunk). butt    — ends meet with no overlap (butt-welded pipe, B16.9). welded  — joined by weld with no mechanical overlap.

embed_depth_m.description: Overlap consumed by the joint, in metres. MUST be 0 for flange/butt/welded and > 0 for slip-fit/socket.

gap_tolerance_m.description: Permitted gap at the joint, in metres.

provenance.description: Where embed_depth comes from. STANDARD for values read off B16.11 etc.; INFER for shop practice; CERT only if measured in the COB drawings — which so far has never been possible, since the drawings are line-work with no joint detail.

instanceable.description: true if geometry is shared across instances (InstancedMesh)

cob_usage.description: How often this part actually occurs in COB level 4, from the inventory. Drives instancing priority and bill-of-quantities.

population.description: MANDATORY when n is present: what n is counted over.
